subject: social
name: Social Studies
course: Ancient Civilizations of the Eastern Hemisphere
title: Grade 6 Social Studies: Ancient Civilizations of the Eastern Hemisphere
overview: Grade 6 Social Studies engages students in historical inquiry, primary source analysis, geographic mapping, and civic deliberation aligned with the C3 Framework.
competencies: Corroborate primary documents with historical context and point-of-view analysis.
Explain how geographical trade networks and physical barriers shaped civilizations.
Analyze economic developments, resource allocation, and market exchanges.
Assess the evolution of democratic values, civil liberties, and civic responsibilities.

modules.title: Early Civilizations of the Fertile Crescent & Nile Valley
modules.description: Examining the Agricultural Revolution, urban innovation, written legal codes in Mesopotamia, and dynastic Egypt.

topics.title: Mesopotamia, Sumer and the Code of Hammurabi
topics.description: Analyzing irrigation engineering, cuneiform writing, city-states, and ancient legal justice.

topics.title: Ancient Egypt: Religion, Monuments and Nile Geography
topics.description: Investigating pharaonic theocracy, pyramid engineering, hieroglyphic records, and trade corridors.

modules.title: Classical India, Ancient China & the Silk Road
modules.description: Exploring the Indus Valley civilization, Maurya and Gupta Empires, Chinese dynasties (Shang, Zhou, Han), and early Silk Road trade.

topics.title: Indus Valley and Classical South Asia
topics.description: Urban planning in Harappa/Mohenjo-Daro, development of Hinduism and Buddhism, and Ashoka's pillars.

topics.title: Dynastic China and Confucian Philosophy
topics.description: The Mandate of Heaven, Confucian and Daoist philosophy, the Great Wall, and Han technological innovations.

modules.title: Classical Mediterranean: Greece and the Roman Republic/Empire
modules.description: Analyzing Athenian direct democracy, Spartan militarism, the Hellenistic age, and the rise and fall of Rome.

topics.title: Ancient Greece: Democracy, Philosophy and Culture
topics.description: Comparing Athens and Sparta, Greek philosophy (Socrates, Plato), drama, and the Olympic games.

topics.title: The Roman Republic and Imperial Expansion
topics.description: The Twelve Tables, republican governance, the transition to empire under Augustus, and Pax Romana.
